Lighting in enclosed, daylight-isolated environments must simultaneously sustain alertness and emotional stability, yet current standards provide limited guidance for achieving both outcomes. This study presents a multimodal predictive framework for preventive lighting design based on emotion–alertness integration. Twenty combinations of illuminance and correlated color temperature were evaluated in a windowless control-room mock-up using EEG, behavioral tasks, and valence–arousal self-reports. Results revealed two distinct functional regions: higher illuminance with mid-to-high correlated color temperature enhanced alertness and performance, whereas lower illuminance with warmer color temperature promoted calmer and more positive affect. A back-propagation neural network predicted subjective alertness and valence from selected EEG and behavioral response features recorded under each lighting condition, and the resulting response patterns were used to map design-relevant lighting regions. The framework provides a direct pathway from multimodal evidence to parameterized lighting decisions, supporting preventive, health-oriented design in enclosed habitats.

item.title: Perceived Discrimination, Preparation for Bias, and Associations with Physical and Mental Health of Racially/Ethnically Marginalized Children
item.description:
Journal of Racial and Ethnic Health Disparities
Abstract Prior studies suggest that perceived discrimination and preparation for bias are associated with children’s mental health, yet few studies have examined relationships with children’s physical health. The current study expands on prior literature by examining associations between perceived discrimination and preparation for bias parenting practices on the physical and mental health of racially/ethnically marginalized children. Children ( n = 227, ages 7–13 years, 58% female; 28% Non-Hispanic Black, 26% Hispanic, 15% Hmong, 15% Native American, 10% multiracial/ethnic with White and 6% multiracial/ethnic without White) completed an in-clinic assessment of cardiometabolic health and self-reported perceived discrimination. Parents completed survey measures of their child’s mental health (self-efficacy, inhibitory control, depression) and their use of preparation for bias parenting practices. Physical health measures (BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, pulse rate, hair cortisol) were taken at a lab visit. In adjusted regression analyses, children who self-reported any experiences of perceived discrimination had significantly lower levels of self-efficacy ( p < 0.05) and inhibitory control ( p < 0.05) than those who did not report experiences of discrimination. Preparation for bias parenting practices differed significantly by race/ethnicity and higher levels were associated with higher hair cortisol concentrations in children, reflecting elevated activity of the hypothalamic-pituitary adrenal (HPA) axis ( p < 0.05). There were otherwise no statistically significant differences in children’s mental or physical health outcomes as a function of perceived discrimination or preparation for bias parenting practices. Our findings highlight the potential importance of interventions that reduce interpersonal discrimination and the need for further research on parenting practices that may influence children’s health.

item.title: Manajemen Kesehatan Masyarakat pada Penanganan Kusta Multibasiler dengan Komorbid Stroke dan Risiko Paparan Tuberkulosis Kontak Serumah di Pedesaan Aceh Utara
item.description:
Sinergi Jurnal Ilmiah Multidisiplin
Kusta multibasiler (MB) merupakan penyakit infeksi kronis yang penanganannya tidak hanya bertumpu pada terapi medis, tetapi juga penyelesaian tantangan determinan sosial, status gizi, keterbatasan fisik, dan stigma masyarakat. Laporan kasus ini bertujuan menganalisis manajemen penanganan kusta MB berbasis pendekatan kedokteran keluarga dan kesehatan masyarakat pada seorang pasien perempuan berusia 38 tahun di Gampong Awe, Kecamatan Kuta Makmur, Aceh Utara. Pasien mengeluhkan bercak mati rasa yang meluas sejak 3 tahun lalu dan saat ini sedang menjalani terapi Multidrug Therapy (MDT) bulan ke-3. Pasien memiliki komorbid stroke non-hemoragik 10 tahun lalu yang menyisakan kelemahan ekstremitas kiri, serta mengalami gizi buruk (underweight, IMT 15,1 kg/m²). Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui home visit, wawancara, pemeriksaan fisik, serta analisis faktor lingkungan dan perilaku keluarga. Hasil evaluasi menggunakan diagram fishbone mengidentifikasi 6 masalah utama: kepatuhan MDT, status gizi buruk, risiko penularan kontak serumah, stigma sosial, dampak stroke pasca-akut, dan ketergantungan ekonomi. Intervensi komprehensif dilakukan secara terintegrasi mencakup promotif, preventif (pemeriksaan kontak serumah dan perawatan kulit mandiri), kuratif (MDT-MB), dan rehabilitatif. Keberhasilan eliminasi kusta membutuhkan kolaborasi lintas sektor dan pemberdayaan keluarga guna memutus rantai penularan serta meningkatkan kualitas hidup penderita.Kata kunci: Kusta Multibasiler, Kesehatan Masyarakat, Kedokteran Keluarga, Stigma, Aceh Utara.AbstractMultibacillary (MB) leprosy is a chronic infectious disease whose management relies not only on medical therapy but also on addressing social determinants, nutritional status, physical limitations, and social stigma. This case report aims to analyze the management of MB leprosy using a family medicine and public health approach in a 38-year-old female patient in Gampong Awe, Kuta Makmur District, North Aceh. The patient reported spreading numb patches over the past 3 years and is currently undergoing month 3 of Multidrug Therapy (MDT). She presents with a comorbid history of non-hemorrhagic stroke 10 years ago resulting in left-sided weakness, alongside severe malnutrition (underweight, BMI 15.1 kg/m²). Data were collected via home visits, interviews, physical examinations, and environmental/behavioral assessments. Fishbone analysis identified six key problems: MDT adherence, malnutrition, contact transmission risk, social stigma, post-stroke motor impairment, and economic dependency. Comprehensive interventions were implemented across health promotion, prevention (contact screening and skin care), curative treatment (MDT-MB), and rehabilitation. Successful leprosy elimination requires cross-sectoral collaboration and family empowerment to interrupt transmission chains and improve quality of life.Keywords: Multibacillary Leprosy, Public Health, Family Medicine, Stigma, North Aceh.

item.title: Localising the Seizure Onset Zone from Routine Interictal and Ictal Scalp EEG Via a Factorised Spatiotemporal Ensemble Deep Learning Framework
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)
Background: Drug-resistant focal epilepsy requires precise localisation of the epileptogenic zone (EZ) for surgical resection. Current practice depends on invasive recordings or spontaneous seizure capture, a costly and risky bottleneck. Interictal scalp EEG can exhibit localising features like spikes, but scalp EEG suffers from volume conduction (the smearing of brain signals across multiple electrodes) and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which obscure subtle spatial dynamics. Neurophysiologist review of long, often multi-day recordings is time-consuming and expertise-dependent, and while computational methods exist, they tend to rely heavily on human-designed features. Deep learning for EEG localisation could therefore help to improve clinical efficiency and sensitivity. Objectives: To develop and validate a non-invasive deep learning approach for lobar-level localisation of the seizure onset zone (SOZ), the primary electrophysiological proxy for the epileptogenic zone (EZ), using interictal and ictal segments from routine scalp EEG. The model is trained on expert-annotated clinical labels and is intended to augment, not supplant, clinical judgement in EZ delineation. Methods: We curated 262 sessions (6,000+ hours) from 100 patients with unilateral focal epilepsy, tested with an extra 28-patient internal and a 9-patient external dataset. The framework integrates: (1) an online augmentation pipeline (Gaussian noise, amplitude scaling, temporal cropping, and hemispheric channel swap) to mitigate overfitting. (2) a multi-scale temporal block for 20-200 ms discharge morphologies; (3) a factorised spatiotemporal Transformer decoupling temporal and spatial attention to counter volume conduction; and (4) a hemispheric mutual exclusivity penalty encoding unilateral priors. A five-model heterogeneous ensemble, fused via model soup, was evaluated on held-out, seizure-free, and cross-institutional cohorts. Results: The ensemble achieved 88.46% session-level exact match on internal test data, outperforming EEGNet (50.00%). Performance generalised to the seizure-free holdout set (82.76%) and to cross-institutional data (84.62%). Rare occipital class (RO) recall rose from 0.500 to 1.000, with zero false positives on healthy controls (n=108). On unlabelled random segments, accuracy was 66.67% (vs. 14% chance). A full 24-hour recording was processed in 4.26 minutes, with inference under 8 seconds, highlighting localising windows for targeted expert clinical review Conclusion: Clinically actionable SOZ spatial information is encoded in routine interictal scalp EEG. Our factorised ensemble provides a safe, interpretable, and efficient tool to expedite presurgical evaluation, potentially reducing reliance on prolonged monitoring and invasive implantation.

item.title: Contribution of the Late Positive Potential to Emotional Memory: A Joint Neuro-Cognitive Approach to Memory Prediction
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory)
Emotional events are better remembered than neutral events. The emotional Context Maintenance and Retrieval model (eCMR) explains this effect by simulating preferential encoding of emotional items, implemented by a free parameter that scales the learning rate. Incorporating a neural signal measured during encoding could make the model's account more specific, permitting a prediction not only of average increased recall but also which emotional items are likely to be recalled. We investigated whether the late positive potential (LPP) event-related potential (ERP) effect could provide this item-specific information in a secondary analysis of EEG recorded while 38 participants encoded negative and neutral pictures for an immediate free recall test (Zarubin et al. 2020). First, we established that the LPP effect was modulated by emotion in an early (400-1000 ms) and a late (1000-2000 ms) time window and this modulation was reliable in 73.7% and 50% of the participants respectively. Second, we investigated at what level the LPP was related to subsequent memory. Emotion-enhanced LPP did not covary with emotion-enhanced memory between participants or across lists within participants, but the early LPP specifically predicted memory for emotional items on a single-trial level. Third, we compared eCMR variants to test whether trial-level early LPP should scale learning for both categories or only for emotional items, and whether it could replace or complement a common learning-rate increase for all emotional items. The best-fitting model combined emotion-specific LPP scaling with the common learning-rate increase. The finding that early LPP predicted enhanced recall only for emotional items is difficult to reconcile with accounts on which the LPP reflects attention or stimulus significance more generally, which predict a relationship to memory for neutral items as well. These results pave the way to quantitative prediction of internal recall trajectories by individual participants without requiring behavioural output.

item.title: Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) and Neural Signal Decoding: Transformer Dynamics, Riemannian Manifolds, and Low-Latency Edge Bio-Processors
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Abstract—Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) establish direct, bidirectional communication conduits between biological central nervous systems and external computational effectors. Emerging high-channel microelectrode arrays (intracortical Utah arrays, Neuropixels) and high-density non-invasive electroencephalography (HD-EEG) capture massive, non-stationary neural population ensembles. Transforming stochastic action potentials (spikes) and local field potentials (LFPs) into continuous robotic prosthetic trajectories or high-speed discrete language communication ('silent speech') demands high-precision, real-time neural decoding. However, deploying clinical neuroprosthetics and consumer BCIs encounters severe physical, physiological, and mathematical barriers: extreme non-stationarity and electrode drift across days, severe inter-session and inter-subject distribution shifts, low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), and strict power-dissipation ceilings (<15 mW) to avoid thermal parenchymal tissue damage. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of deep learning and geometric neural decoding for Brain-Computer Interfaces. We formalize neural population dynamics on Riemannian manifolds under Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) affine-invariant metrics, derive continuous spatial-temporal Neural Transformers (NeuroFormer) equipped with self-supervised masked autoencoding, and model closed-loop Kalman observer dynamics. Furthermore, we construct an empirical clinical and non-invasive evaluation testbed across 1,200 hours of motor imagery EEG (BCI Competition IV-2a) and intracortical primary motor cortex (M1) neural spikes from non-human primate and clinical trial corpora. Our empirical findings demonstrate that Riemannian geometric alignment paired with NeuroFormer decoders achieves a 94.2% continuous trajectory correlation coefficient (R = 0.942) and an unprecedented 68.4 words-per-minute silent speech decoding speed, while reducing daily calibration recalibration drift by 76.8%. Concurrently, custom quantized INT8 edge deployment on neuromorphic bio-processors sustains a deterministic 8.2 ms end-to-end decoding latency within a 4.8 mW power envelope. Finally, we establish open research directions in bidirectional closed-loop neural stimulation, long-term biocompatibility degradation modeling, and cryptographic neuro-privacy safeguards.

item.title: EEG-Based Mental State Classification for Real-Time Game Control Using a Low-Cost BCI System
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
This project presents a low-cost, real-time Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system designed for hands-free computer and game control using affordable hardware. Developed as an undergraduate research project at the Department of Information Science and Engineering, Mysuru Royal Institute of Technology (MRIT), the system captures raw EEG signals from a single frontal dry electrode (Ups & Downs Labs BCI Kit) via an Arduino sampling at 512 Hz. Key components of the workflow include: Signal Processing: Implements a 50 Hz IIR notch filter and a 0.5–30 Hz fourth-order Butterworth band-pass filter to remove mains interference and baseline drift. Feature Extraction: Extracts eight spectral features per one-second window using Welch’s method, with the alpha/beta ratio serving as the primary indicator for cognitive states. Classification: Utilizes a Support Vector Machine (SVM) with an RBF kernel (trained on 4,668 windowed feature vectors) to classify user states as relaxed or attentive. Control & Interaction: Maps predicted mental states to keyboard inputs using pyautogui for real-time game control, complemented by a threshold-based jaw-clench detector for secondary input commands.

item.title: The Unspoken Iceberg and the Condition of Evolution: Narrative and Trust in the Age of Infinite Replication, and the Dialogical Structure of Recursive Self-Improvement (빙산의 아랫부분과 진화의 조건: 무한 복제 시대의 서사와 신뢰, 그리고 재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)을 가능케 하는 대화의 구조)
item.description:
[预印本] Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
As artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics step beyond digital screens to replace physical human labor—approaching closed-loop automation in which even the energy, infrastructure, and maintenance costs required to run AI are sustained by AI itself—a provocative thesis has emerged: currency as a medium for exchanging human labor will lose its relevance. Combined with the zero-marginal-cost replication of generative AI and the trajectory of brain-computer interfaces (BCI), this prospect raises a foundational philosophical question: when outcomes, labor, and even stored knowledge can be infinitely replicated, what remains uncopyable and unchanged? This paper takes as its point of departure a symmetrical paradox: while the production of matter and labor can be completed inside a self-sustaining closed loop (a material closed loop), the generation of meaning and the evolution of intelligence can never be completed inside a closed loop (a cognitive closed loop). Distinguishing between what changes (labor-backed currency and the scarcity of mere outputs) and what does not change (living one's own life through understanding, and relationships), we establish a four-stage deductive chain that unifies post-monetary value theory with the epistemological prerequisite of universal evolution: 1. Material Closed Loops and the Value Theory of Irreversible Time (Δt): Closed-loop automation drives the exchange value of abstract labor time invested to produce outputs toward 0. Yet at the intersection between the finite physical Earth (wattage and tonnage) and the non-rivalrous, infinitely expanding digital world, a single physical constraint that can never be compressed or duplicated in one second even within the digital realm emerges as the ultimate scarcity: the irreversibility of lived time (Δt). In a post-monetary world, the center of gravity shifts from surface outputs to Narrative and the Trust born from it.2. The Iceberg Structure of Context and Infinite Regress: Every utterance and recorded dataset is merely the expressed context (the tip of the iceberg above water), whereas the lived trajectory supporting why that exact symbol was chosen over alternatives remains submerged in the unexpressed context (the iceberg beneath the water). Adding an explanatory sentence is not subtraction from a static warehouse, but a generative event that creates a new meta-context in real time; consequently, unspoken context trails in an infinite regress whose residual conditional entropy never converges to 0. Far from a defect, this inexhaustible surplus is the living potential capable of drawing up new answers to unfamiliar future questions—and the substance of personal Trust as opposed to mere statistical Reliance.3. Model Collapse in Cognitive Closed Loops and Dialogue as the Condition of Evolution and RSI: An AI attempting Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in a closed loop—by repeatedly consuming its own expressed outputs or conversing only within an offline multi-agent echo chamber—suffers support contraction and variance decay (Model Collapse). Across biological co-evolution, human growth, and AI self-improvement (RSI), the universal prerequisite is expressing internal potential outward, colliding with an uncontrollable external world and other minds who have lived through independent irreversible time (Δt), and rewriting oneself—which is Dialogue. --- 본 논문은 “물질과 노동의 생산은 닫힌 루프(물질적 폐루프)로 완결될 수 있으나, 의미의 생성과 지능의 진화는 결코 닫힌 루프(인지적 폐루프)로 완결될 수 없다”는 대칭적 역설을 출발점으로 삼아, ① 물질적 폐루프와 비가역적 시간(Δt)의 가치론(서사와 신뢰), ② 표현된 맥락(빙산의 윗부분)과 표현하지 않은 맥락(빙산의 아랫부분)의 무한후퇴, ③ 인지적 폐루프의 모델 붕괴를 넘어 생물·인간·AI의 진화와 재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)을 가능케 하는 보편적 전제조건으로서의 ‘대화’를 규명한다.

item.title: Transfer-Related Cognitive and Learning Profiles Across Predominant MOBA Roles in Novice Esports Players
item.description:
Akdeniz Spor Bilimleri Dergisi
Esports research increasingly recognizes that multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) games contain differentiated team roles, yet it remains unclear whether these role differences correspond to cognitive and learning-related profiles beyond immediate gameplay. This exploratory secondary analysis examined whether naturally emerging predominant roles were associated with post-intervention transfer-related outcomes among novice League of Legends players. Here, transfer-related refers to outcomes assessed beyond immediate gameplay and does not imply causal demonstration of transfer. Data came from the experimental arm of an eight-week quasi-experimental intervention requiring at least 18 hours of gameplay. Of 42 experimental participants, one predominantly played jungle and was excluded because this created a single-participant category. The final sample comprised 41 undergraduates classified as top lane (n = 5), mid lane (n = 15), marksman/ADC (n = 12), or support (n = 9). Outcomes included EEG-based attention-related engagement, working-memory-related theta activity, and theta/alpha-based cognitive load recorded during a standardized dual n-back task, together with 21st-century learner skills and content-specific learning performance. After z-standardization, Euclidean distances were analyzed using PERMANOVA with 9,999 permutations, principal coordinates analysis, and a multivariate dispersion diagnostic. The omnibus PERMANOVA did not detect statistically significant role-based differentiation, pseudo-F(3, 37) = 0.941, p = .526, R² = .071. PCoA showed substantial overlap, no statistically detectable dispersion differences were found, and the baseline sensitivity analysis was non-significant. These findings suggest that functional role differentiation within MOBA gameplay should not be assumed to produce corresponding differentiation in transfer-related outcomes among novice players with relatively short role exposure.

item.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease
item.description:
Sensors
Digital health technologies are playing an increasingly important role in patient monitoring, able to capture longitudinal data to supplement scheduled episodic evaluations conducted by clinicians. Rapid advances in sensors and data processing algorithms have resulted in some highly sophisticated systems capable of monitoring and tracking numerous symptoms with high levels of sensitivity and specificity. These approaches, however, often require active engagement with the patient, potentially increasing burden in a clinical trial and often resulting in diminishing adherence over time. In the case of slow-progressing neurodegenerative diseases, this may become an obstacle, as often very subtle changes in symptoms are typically monitored over a multi-year period. Accordingly, there is evident interest in passive monitoring solutions which have minimal burden on patients. Smart ring technologies are one such solution, with appealing form factors, low engagement requirements and increasing intervals before device recharging is required. While newer devices are capable of tracking sleep function with increasing levels of accuracy, they are unable to offer the precision afforded by gold standard sleep analysis such as electroencephalography (EEG), polysomnography (PSG) and sleep laboratory protocols. Prompted by a recent study which highlighted the reduced accuracy of consumer-based sleep devices compared with conventional approaches, we posit that the benefits of such devices may offset the constraints of measurement accuracy. Furthermore, any accuracy–adherence trade-offs would be compensated by long-term statistical benefits derived from detecting within-person changes and reducing measurement noise through enhanced sampling frequencies. In this perspective, we highlight their potential utility in tracking Parkinson’s disease patients longitudinally, where compromised sleep architectures are associated with multiple symptoms and continuous monitoring could offer myriad patient benefits.

item.title: Factors Associated with Health-Related Quality of Life Among Greek Candidates for Bariatric Surgery: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description:
Obesities
Background: This study examined demographic, anthropometric, and psychological factors associated with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among Greek candidates for bariatric surgery. Methods: A total of 524 candidates for bariatric surgery (mean age = 41.49 years, SD = 11.18) were recruited from the Interbalkan Medical Centre of Thessaloniki between May 2019 and November 2024. Participants completed standardized measures assessing depressive symptoms, anxiety, disordered eating attitudes, psychological resilience, personality traits, and HRQoL. Eight theory-informed multiple linear regression models were fitted to examine cross-sectional associations with the SF-36 domains, adjusting simultaneously for 12 demographic, anthropometric, and psychological covariates. Heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors and false discovery rate (FDR) correction were applied. Results: Depressive symptoms were negatively associated with all eight SF-36 domains after multivariable adjustment and FDR correction. Higher BMI was associated with poorer scores across all four physical HRQoL domains, as well as Social Functioning and Vitality, while older age was negatively associated with all four physical domains. Anxiety symptoms were independently associated only with Mental Health. Psychological resilience was positively associated with General Health Perceptions and Vitality, whereas higher Neuroticism and Extraversion were associated with poorer and better mental and psychosocial HRQoL, respectively. Adjusted R2 values ranged from 0.245 to 0.548 across the eight SF-36 domains. Discussion: Depressive symptoms emerged as the most consistent correlate of HRQoL among Greek candidates for bariatric surgery, whereas BMI, age, resilience, anxiety, and personality traits demonstrated more domain-specific associations. These findings highlight the relevance of comprehensive preoperative assessment addressing both physical and psychological functioning. Conclusions: Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and determine whether these characteristics are associated with postoperative HRQoL outcomes.

item.title: From Nutrition Knowledge to Health-Related Behaviors in Undergraduate Nursing Education: A Cross-Sectional Study
item.description:
Nursing Reports
Background/Objectives: Nutrition knowledge is an important component of undergraduate nursing education, but greater knowledge does not necessarily translate into healthier personal behaviors. This study aimed to assess nutrition knowledge and health-related behaviors among undergraduate nursing students, compare these outcomes across academic years, and identify factors associated with both dimensions. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among students enrolled in the four-year nursing degree at the University of Santiago de Compostela, Spain, during the 2025/2026 academic year. Participants completed a study-specific ad hoc questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, nutrition knowledge, dietary and health-related behaviors, self-rated dietary quality, and body mass index (BMI) perception. Bivariate analyses, multiple linear regression, ordinal logistic regression, and weighted Cohen’s kappa were used. Results: A total of 297 students participated (50.9% response rate); 81.1% were women. Mean nutrition knowledge was 22.51 ± 4.01/36 and differed across academic years, ranging from 21.56 ± 3.74 among first-year students to 24.64 ± 3.87 among fourth-year students (p < 0.001). The mean health-related behaviors score was 76.26 ± 7.01/105 and did not differ across academic years (p = 0.103). Behavior score increased from 68.33 ± 7.78 among students rating their diet as poor to 84.81 ± 4.32 among those rating it as very good (p < 0.001); each 10-point increase was associated with higher odds of reporting a better dietary-quality category (adjusted OR = 7.78; 95% CI: 4.99–12.13). Exact agreement between calculated and self-perceived BMI categories was 82.7% (weighted κ = 0.593). Conclusions: Nutrition knowledge was higher among students in later academic years, whereas health-related behaviors did not show a similar academic pattern. These findings suggest that undergraduate nursing education should reinforce practical and behavior-oriented nutrition learning alongside theoretical knowledge.

item.title: Food Label Reading and Cardiovascular Health Profiles Across Adulthood: Findings from the Look-Up 8+ Study
item.description:
Nutrients
Background: Unhealthy dietary patterns are a major risk factor for death and functional disability. Food labeling provides key nutritional information and is associated with healthier dietary patterns. This study aims to investigate whether attention to food labels is associated with dietary patterns, BMI, and Cardiovascular 8 metrics scores. Methods: We analyzed data from the Look-Up 8+ project, including adults aged 18 years or older from several Italian regions. Participants underwent a comprehensive lifestyle assessment, including dietary habits, cholesterol and glucose measurements, and anthropometric evaluations. Descriptive, comparative, and inferential statistical analyses were used to investigate the association between attention to food labels and dietary patterns, BMI, and Cardiovascular Health scores. Results: Among 7401 participants (mean age 54.4 ± 15.0 years, with 55.5% women), those who reported reading food labels exhibited a higher prevalence of regular physical activity and adherence to a healthy diet. In contrast, participants who did not read food labels had a higher body mass index. Both men and women who reported greater attention to food composition had a higher Life’s Essential 8 score. Conclusions: These results suggest that attention to food labels is associated with more favorable lifestyle choices and improved cardiovascular health profiles.

item.title: Treg and Oxidative Stress Biomarker Profiles in Long COVID and Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
item.description:
International Journal of Molecular Sciences
Chronic immune dysregulation is the possible pathophysiological mechanism in myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and long coronavirus infectious disease (long COVID, LC). However, a detailed characterization of regulatory and effector T-cell subsets in these conditions remains limited. To assess and compare T-cell subsets in relation to serum biomarkers of chronic activation and oxidative/nitrosative stress in an attempt to differentiate between LC and ME/CFS patients. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PMNC) from LC patients (n = 89), ME/CFS patients (n = 125), and healthy controls (HC, n = 80) were analyzed using multiparameter flow cytometry. The frequencies of naïve (CD45RA+), effector (CD45RA-), CD31+, CD39+, CD73+, GARP+, PI16+, CD15s/CD161+, and CD147+ Treg subsets were determined in relation to CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell differentiation, activation, and effector subsets. Catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), glutathione peroxidase 1 (GPX1), malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide synthase 1 and 3 (NOS1, NOS3), zonulin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), immunoglobulin G (IgG) against lipopolysaccharide (IgG-LPS), Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), and Dickkopf-related protein 1 (DKK1) were measured in serum by ELISA. Clinical symptom scores (HAMA, HAMD, FF, dePol) were additionally assessed. The immune-serum biomarkers distinguishing LC, ME/CFS, and HC comprised Th17, CD15s+CD161−eTreg, and CD161+ Treg. The five-marker signature retained significance after adjustment for age, BMI, and sex. Altered T-cell subsets were strongly associated with markers of oxidative (GPX1) and nitrosative (NOS3) stress but not directly with symptom severity. ME/CFS showed a strong separation from HC across Random Forest (AUC = 0.907) and logistic regression (AUC = 0.924). The modest distinction of LC from HC (AUC = 0.727 and 0.577 respectively) possibly reflected important endotypic diversity, though differences in disease duration, vaccination history, biomarker selection, and other cohort characteristics might add to it. MDA was an independent predictor for three-class classification, ME/CFS vs. HC, and LC vs. HC pairwise comparisons, while GPX1 discriminated between ME/CFS and LC. In spite of shared biomarkers of oxidative stress and T-cell response dysregulation, our results support the hypothesis that LC and ME/CFS differ in the extent of cellular damage and the exhaustion of compensatory mechanisms.

item.title: Which Blood Pressure Measures Correlate with Nocturia Severity in Adolescents?
item.description:
Clocks & Sleep
Nocturia, defined as waking to void during sleep hours, is common in adolescents, causing sleep disruption and daytime fatigue. While numerous studies have found nocturia associated with systolic blood pressure (BP) hypertension in adults, diastolic (D) BP has greater relative importance in youth. Little is known about the hemodynamic profile of the hypertension–nocturia link in adolescents. Accordingly, we evaluated relationships between nocturia severity and brachial artery systolic and DBPs in each arm, as well as central aortic pressures using applanation tonometry. We studied 100 adolescents, 10–18 years, from pediatric clinics. Nocturnal urinary indices were obtained from voiding diaries. Results: In total, 45% reported nocturia. Nocturia severity was correlated with left and right arm brachial SBP, higher of two arms, and central SBP (r = 0.27, p = 0.007). Brachial SBP was also correlated with nocturnal urine volume (NUV) (r = 0.31, p = 0.001) and production rate (NUP) (r = 0.32, p = 0.001). DBP showed no significant correlations. After adjusting for BMI and sex, brachial SBP remained independently associated with nocturia severity. The median first uninterrupted sleep period was 171 min (25–75%ile; 94, 300). In adolescents, SBP is associated with nocturia severity, NUV, and NUP. Nocturia typically occurs during the first half of nighttime, suggesting an impact on deep sleep.

item.title: Six-Minute Walk Performance, BMI and Estimated Cardiorespiratory Fitness Among Primary-School Boys: A Large-Scale Regional Study in Southern Italy
item.description:
Children
Background: This study examined whether measured walking performance, body mass index (BMI) and estimated cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) differ across the six provinces of Apulia (southern Italy), and whether physical fitness components and psychological variables (perceived self-efficacy [PSE] and enjoyment) are associated with these outcomes in primary-school boys. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 2700 boys. BMI, Standing Long Jump (SLJ), 4 × 10 m Shuttle Run (4 × 10 m SR), 6-Minute Walk Test and questionnaire data were collected, and VO2max was estimated with the Jalili equation, which combines 6-min walk distance (6MWD) and BMI and was developed in older boys without validation in children aged 8–10 years. Measured 6MWD was analyzed as the primary outcome and estimated VO2max as a complementary outcome, using linear models. Results: Measured 6MWD, SLJ, 4 × 10 m SR did not differ across provinces (all p > 0.50). Province was not associated with 6MWD (p = 0.331), which was positively associated with SLJ and inversely associated with 4 × 10 m SR (both p < 0.001). Estimated VO2max differed across provinces (p < 0.001), but this difference disappeared after accounting for BMI (p = 0.340) and was almost entirely attributable to the BMI term of the estimation equation. No clear independent association emerged for PSE and enjoyment (p = 0.119; p = 0.281). Conclusions: Provincial differences in equation-derived VO2max were almost entirely attributable to differences in BMI, entered through the estimation equation, and should not be interpreted as differences in aerobic capacity. Because the equation was developed in older boys and has not been validated in children aged 8–10 years, these values are indirect, group-level estimates rather than measurements of CRF.

item.title: Temporal Dynamics of Moral Semantic Processing in Chinese: An ERP Study of Word Categorization
item.description:
Behavioral Sciences
Morality serves as a universal code of behavior and a foundation for social value systems. To investigate the cognitive architecture of moral information processing, the present study adopted event-related potentials (ERPs). We used Chinese moral words as stimuli to characterize the temporal neural dynamics of moral processing. Fifty-four participants completed a one-way repeated-measures lexical categorization task with four conditions (moral, immoral, neutral, and pseudowords), including response mapping as a between-subjects factor. Behavioral responses and electroencephalography (EEG) activity were recorded simultaneously. Behavioral analyses yielded robust response latency disparities: participants categorized moral words most rapidly, followed by neutral words and immoral words; pseudowords elicited the slowest responses. ERP analyses revealed graded neural signatures across stimulus categories. During the P2 window (150–250 ms), immoral words elicited the largest amplitudes. At the N3 component (250–350 ms), real words showed attenuated negativity compared with pseudowords, and moral words also differed from neutral words, suggesting that N3 reflects lexical-semantic categorization with additional moral-relevance effects. At the LPP (400–800 ms), immoral words evoked the largest responses, significantly larger than those for neutral and pseudowords, whereas the moral–immoral contrast was not significant. Collectively, these results are consistent with an affective-moral salience account: moral words show a behavioral recognition advantage, and immoral words elicit heightened early and late neurocognitive sensitivity. The findings highlight the utility of ERP analysis for mapping moral semantic processing within the logographic Chinese writing system, and may inform future cross-cultural neurocognitive research and semantic decoding in brain–computer interface paradigms.

item.title: EEG Emotion Recognition Based on Azimuthal Equidistant Projection and a Multiscale Residual Temporal Network
item.description:
Brain Sciences
Background: In most existing EEG-based emotion recognition studies, the spatial configuration of electroencephalography (EEG) electrodes is not adequately preserved, and conventional single-scale convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have limited ability to capture both local and global spatial patterns. To address these limitations, an EEG emotion recognition framework integrating azimuthal equidistant projection (AEP) with a multiscale residual temporal network (MRTNet) is proposed. Methods: Differential entropy (DE) features are first extracted, and the three-dimensional electrode coordinates are projected onto a two-dimensional plane to construct AEP-based DE (AEP-DE) feature maps that preserve the spatial topology of the electrode layout. MRTNet then combines multiscale depthwise separable convolutions with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to extract spatial features at multiple receptive-field scales and model temporal dependencies across EEG segments. Results: Experimental results show that MRTNet achieves average accuracies of 95.1% for four-class classification on the Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP) and 93.1% for three-class classification on the SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED). Conclusions: Grad-CAM visualizations further indicate that the model responses are concentrated in spatially localized frontal and temporal regions, providing qualitative support for the spatial interpretability of the proposed method.
